newsitem.title: UK: Equitas says premium reduced to 11.2 billion stg.
newsitem.headline: Equitas says premium reduced to 11.2 billion stg.

text.p: David Newbigging, the chairman of Equitas, the company created to run-off Lloyd's of London's huge pre-1993 liabilities, described its first five months as a case of "so far, so good" on Monday as the company published its first set of accounts.

The payment of claims and expenses by syndicates last year had reduced its reinsurance premium to 11.2 billion pounds ($18.3 billion) by the time it began operating in September last year, down from a figure of 14.7 billion based on year-end 1995 figures.
The company said that by September the group had assets totalling 16 billion pounds and net claims reserves of 10.5 billion pounds.

Newbigging said Equitas had two clearly defined objectives - to secure true finality for Reinsured Names, individuals who have traditionally supported the insurance market, and to create a sufficient surplus to enable some return of the premium to them.
But he said neither of these targets would be easy.
However, there had been no major surprises so far, he said, and the position of the group today "is much as we anticipated at the time we became operational".
The Corporation of Lloyd's is collecting the premium for Equitas and by December 1996 around 95 percent of the premium receivable had been collected.

Equitas was formed to allow a line to be drawn under the near-disastrous losses which at one point threatened to destroy Lloyd's and was a central plank of the "Reconstruction & Renewal" plan implemented last year.
